payload.text: THE BASH TOOL'S SHELL IS ZSH, AND THE TOOLS ARE BSD'S, AND BOTH BIT ON 2026-09-23. (1) An unquoted `$list` does not word-split, so a loop over paths saw one string. My commit guard refused it, which is the only reason nothing wrong landed. (2) `${PIPESTATUS[0]}` is empty, because zsh spells it `$pipestatus[1]`. (3) A glob that matches nothing aborts the whole command (nomatch). (4) An awk run inside a double-quoted `$(...)` printed nothing over a file it should have flagged -- a page agent's measurement. (5) BSD grep has no `-P`. At this localfold my ASCII check `grep -P ... && fail || true` errored on both files, the `|| true` swallowed the error, and it printed a pass it never measured -- the commit landed on it, and only a re-measure with a control showed the fact happened to hold. (6) A word opening with `=` is zsh's command-path expansion: `echo =====` fails with "===== not found". (7) zsh's `[` has no `<` string comparison: `[ "$a" \< "$b" ]` fails with "condition expected" on every pair, and the loop's own footer, "no line = no overlap", would have read as a clean result; the bash rerun counted its pairs, 6 of 6 (both on 2026-09-23, afternoon). Anything with arrays, word splitting, a string comparison or a pipeline's status runs under `bash <<'BASH' ... BASH`, and any guard is driven red once before its green is read.
